core_obligations: The special case (proof lines 394-400): the author begins with the case of a finite module, where the claim is that a map into a colimit over a limit ordinal factors through one stage, referring to the previously proved lemma for finite objects.

The general reduction (proof lines 402-415): for an arbitrary module and a map into the colimit, smallness is reduced to showing that the preimages of the stages under the map stabilize, one writes the module as the union of the images of the preimages, and this makes the family of preimages a directed family indexed by the ordinal.

Stabilisation (proof lines 416-429): choosing a subset of stages whose preimages cover one fixed preimage and using that there are at most kappa submodules, the subset has cardinality at most kappa and hence an upper bound strictly below the given ordinal, so that the fixed preimage equals the preimage of that bound; consequently the map factors through that stage, which is the claim.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the statement that the preimages of the stages under a map into the colimit stabilize.
Write the module as the union of those preimages to get a directed family.
Use the bound on the number of submodules and the cofinality hypothesis to find an upper bound stage, and read off the factorisation.
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that an R-module with at most kappa submodules is alpha-small with respect to injections for every ordinal alpha whose cofinality exceeds kappa (statement lines 386-392). The proof is a complete argument: the finite case is recalled from a named lemma (proof lines 394-400), the general case is reduced to the stabilisation of the preimages of the stages of the inductive system under a map into the colimit (proof lines 402-415), and stabilisation follows because the set of stages whose preimages cover a fixed one has cardinality at most kappa and therefore has an upper bound strictly below alpha, using the cofinality hypothesis (proof lines 416-429). The non-formal content is the reduction and the cofinality bookkeeping. The claim is H2.
